The `title:` field names the real upstream Apache Hadoop JIRA / git commit. Your job is to reproduce that upstream change as faithfully as you can from the requirement text plus the code you find in the tree.   * log message wording and format placeholders

If the requirement text names an identifier (class, method, config key, metric, constant), use that identifier verbatim.

HOW TO WORK
1. Read the requirement yaml. Note the JIRA id and the module it belongs to (HDFS / YARN / MAPREDUCE / HADOOP-common / tools).
2. Locate the real code with Grep/Glob. Read enough surrounding code (and the existing tests for it) to make a correct, idiomatic change.
3. Implement the change. Match the surrounding code style, license headers, checkstyle habits (2-space indent, 80-col-ish, final where used, LOG placeholders `{}`).
4. If the change adds a config key, also add it to the matching `*-default.xml` (hdfs-default.xml / core-default.xml / yarn-default.xml / mapred-default.xml) with a sensible description, and to the `DFSConfigKeys`/`YarnConfiguration`/etc. constants class the module uses. 5. If the upstream change would have come with tests, add or extend the corresponding test class under the same module (src/test/java/...). Keep tests deterministic and cheap. Do not add tests that need network or a real cluster beyond the usual MiniDFSCluster/MiniYARNCluster idioms already used in that test file.

Instead be rigorous by inspection: every symbol you reference must exist (grep to confirm), every new import must be needed and correct, braces/parens balanced, no stale references left behind. Re-read your own final diff (`git diff -- <your files>`) before finishing and fix anything sloppy.

1	title: HADOOP-18002. abfs rename idempotency broken -remove recovery
2	category: refactor
3	requirement: '## Context
4	
5	  ABFS clients currently try to recover ambiguous rename results by comparing modification times, but operators cannot rely on that signal because rename does not update object modification time. Keeping that recovery path in the client makes rename behavior look safer than it really is and adds unnecessary I/O.
6	
7	
8	  ## Desired outcome
9	
10	  Remove the built-in modtime-based rename recovery path from the ABFS client and keep rename as a direct operation without that false idempotency check. Workloads that need rename recovery should use the etag-based approach outside the client instead of expecting the filesystem to guess the outcome.
11	
12	
13	  ## Acceptance signals
14	
15	  Normal rename scenarios continue to behave the same, but the client no longer performs the deleted modtime recovery logic or advertises that path as the way to recover uncertain rename outcomes.
16	
17	  '
